# LNT v5

> LNT is LLVM's performance-monitoring server. Build bots submit benchmark
> results to it; it stores them as time series and serves them back so that
> performance changes can be found, investigated and tracked. Everything it
> holds is available through the REST API described below.

## Documentation

- [OpenAPI specification](/api/openapi.json): every parameter, request body,
  response body and status code. Consult it for anything this file leaves out.
- [Interactive documentation](/api/docs): the same specification, for humans.
- [API index](/api): links to the project list endpoint and to both of the
  above, and the commit of LNT the server was built from.

## Concepts

- **Project** -- groups the test suites of one software project, such as
  libc++ or Swift. Every suite belongs to exactly one project. A project has a
  `name` and an optional `display_name`. `GET /api/projects` returns every
  project with its suites and their schemas.
- **Test suite** -- a self-contained collection of machines, commits, runs and
  regressions, with a schema of its own. A suite's name is unique within its
  project, so it is identified by both names together, written
  `project/suite` outside the API. Nearly every endpoint lives under
  `/api/projects/{project}/suites/{suite}/`, and nothing is shared between
  suites: two suites may hold machines of the same name and they are different
  machines.
- **Schema** -- a suite declares its `metrics`, `machine_fields` and
  `commit_fields` up front. Each entry has a `name` and a `type`: `real`,
  `integer`, `text` or `datetime`. Nothing undeclared can be stored: a metric or
  a field the schema does not name is rejected with 400 rather than ignored.
  An optional `repository` block holds URL templates of the repository's
  commits (`{commit}`) and of the changes between two commits (`{from}`,
  `{to}`), for clients to link to.
- **Machine** -- where a benchmark ran, addressed by `name`. Carries the
  declared `machine_fields` under `fields`, and a built-in `tracked` flag
  marking whether it takes part in *automatic* machine selection, such as a
  dashboard picking which machines to show.
- **Commit** -- what was benchmarked, addressed by an identity string `value`
  (a Git SHA, a version, or an ad-hoc label like `experiment-vectorizer-v2`).
  Carries the declared `commit_fields` under `fields`, plus two optional
  built-ins: `ordinal`, an integer placing the commit in the suite's total order,
  and `tag`, a label such as `release-18.1`. An ordinal is never inferred, not
  even from a numeric commit string. A series serves a commit without one after
  the commits that have one, and leaves it out of a range of commits. Listing
  commits orders them by when the server first saw each one by default
  (`sort=first_seen`); `sort=-first_seen` puts the most recently seen first.
  `sort=ordinal` (`-ordinal`) orders them by ordinal, followed by the commits
  without one, by when they were first seen in the same direction.
  `has_ordinal=true|false` keeps only the commits with or without an ordinal,
  and `after_commit=` and `before_commit=` bound the list by ordinal, leaving out
  the commits without one.
- **Run** -- one submission of results for one machine at one commit,
  identified by a UUID. Several runs may share a machine and a commit.
- **Test** -- a benchmark name, created implicitly by submission. Test names
  contain `/`, so no path ever carries one: a test is named in a `test=` query
  parameter or in a request body. Machine names and commit values do appear in
  paths, so they may not contain `/` or `%`, or be `.` or `..`.
- **Sample** -- one measurement of one test in one run: `{test, metrics}`, where
  `metrics` holds only the metrics that have a value. A test measured several
  times in one run yields one sample per repetition.
- **Profile** -- optional instruction-level counter data for one test in one
  run. It is submitted inline with the run, as a test entry's `profile`: a JSON
  document, gzip-compressed and base64-encoded. It is read back through its own
  UUID, piecemeal or as that same document in plain JSON.
- **Regression** -- a performance change someone is tracking: a state, and
  optionally a title, a `bug` URL in an external tracker, a suspected commit and
  free-form notes, plus *indicators*, each naming one `(machine, test, metric)`
  the change was observed on. LNT does no detection of its own; an external
  analyzer reads the time series and records what it finds here.

## Endpoints

Every operation, with the scope it requires (see Authentication).

```
GET    /api                                                                  read    API index
GET    /api/auth                                                             read    The API key the request authenticated with
GET    /api/projects                                                         read    Every project, with its suites and their schemas
POST   /api/projects                                                         manage  Create a project (an unrestricted key only)
GET    /api/projects/{project}                                               read    One project, with its suites
PATCH  /api/projects/{project}                                               manage  Rename it (an unrestricted key only), or change its display name
DELETE /api/projects/{project}                                               manage  Delete a project that has no suites (an unrestricted key only)

GET    /api/projects/{project}/suites                                        read    The project's suites, with their schemas
POST   /api/projects/{project}/suites                                        manage  Create a suite in the project from a schema
GET    /api/projects/{project}/suites/{suite}                                read    One suite's schema
PATCH  /api/projects/{project}/suites/{suite}                                manage  Rename a suite, or move it to another project
PATCH  /api/projects/{project}/suites/{suite}/schema                         manage  Add, update or remove metrics and fields, or change the repository
DELETE /api/projects/{project}/suites/{suite}                                manage  Delete a suite and all its data

GET    /api/projects/{project}/suites/{suite}/machines                       read    List machines (search=, tracked=, sort=)
POST   /api/projects/{project}/suites/{suite}/machines                       manage  Create a machine
GET    /api/projects/{project}/suites/{suite}/machines/{machine_name}        read    One machine
PATCH  /api/projects/{project}/suites/{suite}/machines/{machine_name}        manage  Update or rename a machine
DELETE /api/projects/{project}/suites/{suite}/machines/{machine_name}        manage  Delete a machine and its runs

GET    /api/projects/{project}/suites/{suite}/commits                        read    List commits (search=, machine=, commit=, has_ordinal=, before_commit=, sort=, ...)
POST   /api/projects/{project}/suites/{suite}/commits                        submit  Create a commit
POST   /api/projects/{project}/suites/{suite}/commits/resolve                read    Look up many commits by value at once
GET    /api/projects/{project}/suites/{suite}/commits/{value}                read    One commit, with its previous/next by ordinal
PATCH  /api/projects/{project}/suites/{suite}/commits/{value}                manage  Set or clear its ordinal, tag or fields
DELETE /api/projects/{project}/suites/{suite}/commits/{value}                manage  Delete a commit and its runs

GET    /api/projects/{project}/suites/{suite}/runs                           read    List runs (machine=, commit=, search=, sort=, ...)
POST   /api/projects/{project}/suites/{suite}/runs                           submit  Submit a run
GET    /api/projects/{project}/suites/{suite}/runs/{uuid}                    read    One run
DELETE /api/projects/{project}/suites/{suite}/runs/{uuid}                    manage  Delete a run
GET    /api/projects/{project}/suites/{suite}/runs/{uuid}/samples            read    A run's samples (test=)
GET    /api/projects/{project}/suites/{suite}/runs/{uuid}/profiles           read    A run's profiles, as {test, uuid}

GET    /api/projects/{project}/suites/{suite}/tests                          read    List tests (search=, machine=, metric=)

GET    /api/projects/{project}/suites/{suite}/series                         read    A machine's series for one metric, as NDJSON
GET    /api/projects/{project}/suites/{suite}/trends                         read    Per-commit geomeans, per machine

GET    /api/projects/{project}/suites/{suite}/profiles/{uuid}                read    A profile's top-level counters
GET    /api/projects/{project}/suites/{suite}/profiles/{uuid}/functions      read    Its functions, with their counters
GET    /api/projects/{project}/suites/{suite}/profiles/{uuid}/disassembly    read    One function's instructions (function=)
GET    /api/projects/{project}/suites/{suite}/profiles/{uuid}/document       read    The whole profile, as the document a submission carries

GET    /api/projects/{project}/suites/{suite}/regressions                    read    List regressions (state=, machine=, search=, sort=, ...)
POST   /api/projects/{project}/suites/{suite}/regressions                    triage  Create a regression
GET    /api/projects/{project}/suites/{suite}/regressions/{uuid}             read    One regression, with its indicators
PATCH  /api/projects/{project}/suites/{suite}/regressions/{uuid}             triage  Update title, bug, notes, state or commit
DELETE /api/projects/{project}/suites/{suite}/regressions/{uuid}             triage  Delete a regression
POST   /api/projects/{project}/suites/{suite}/regressions/{uuid}/indicators  triage  Add indicators
DELETE /api/projects/{project}/suites/{suite}/regressions/{uuid}/indicators  triage  Remove indicators, by UUID
POST   /api/projects/{project}/suites/{suite}/regressions/indicators/query   read    Indicators across regressions (machine, test, metric, state, commit)

GET    /api/admin/api-keys                                                   admin   List API keys
POST   /api/admin/api-keys                                                   admin   Create an API key
DELETE /api/admin/api-keys/{prefix}                                          admin   Revoke an API key
```

Deleting a suite, or removing entries from its schema, destroys data and needs
`?confirm=true`. Deleting a project destroys nothing, and is refused (409
`conflict`) while it has suites.

## Conventions

- **List endpoints return objects**: `{"items": [...]}`, plus
  `"cursor": {"next": ..., "previous": null}` on a cursor-paginated endpoint,
  whose `limit` defaults to 25, at most 10000. The others return every result.
  Streaming endpoints (`GET /series`) return one JSON object per line instead
  (NDJSON), unpaginated. A failure after the response has started closes the
  connection before its end, which HTTP clients report as an error.
- **Cursors**: send `cursor.next` back unchanged -- as `cursor=`, or as the
  `cursor` key of a request body -- with the same filters and `sort`; only
  `limit` may change. Stop when it is null. Never parse or build one. A cursor
  rejected with `invalid_cursor` (400) means: start again from the first page.
- **Sorting**: `sort=<name>`, prefixed with `-` for descending.
- **Query parameters**: give several values by repeating the parameter
  (`?state=active&state=detected`). A parameter the endpoint does not take is
  400 rather than ignored, and so is repeating one that takes a single value.
- **Errors**: `{"error": {"code": "...", "message": "..."}}`. Branch on `code`,
  never on `message`. The codes are `invalid_request` and `invalid_cursor`
  (400, see Cursors), `unauthorized` (401), `forbidden` (403), `not_found`
  (404), `method_not_allowed` (405, with an `Allow` header), `duplicate`,
  `conflict` and `retry` (409), `unsupported_encoding` (415, see Compression),
  and `internal_error` (500). A request body too large for the deployment is a
  plain-text 413 instead. Among the 409s:
  - `duplicate`: the entity exists. For a run or a regression whose UUID you
    chose, an earlier attempt most likely succeeded: do not resend under a fresh
    UUID, which would store it twice.
  - `conflict`: the request contradicts stored state -- metadata a submission
    disagrees with, or an ordinal another commit holds. Do not retry as sent;
    change the request or the state first.
  - `retry`: a concurrent change to the suite's schema, or to the project, got
    in the way. Nothing was written; send the same request again.
- **Names that match nothing**: a run submission creates the machine, commit
  and tests it names. Everywhere else, an unknown machine or test is 404, an
  unknown metric or regression state is 400, and an unknown commit used as a
  filter (`commit=`, or the `commit` of the indicator lookup) is an empty
  result. A commit used as a range bound (`after_commit`, `before_commit`) is
  404 if unknown and 400 if it has no ordinal. A commit a regression refers to
  is 404. A schema `PATCH` that updates or removes an entry the schema does not
  have is 404, metrics included.
- **Values**: timestamps are ISO 8601 in UTC with a `Z` suffix. Values in
  `fields` and `metrics` use the JSON type their declared type calls for: a
  number for `real` and `integer`, never a string, so `"5"` is not accepted for
  an integer; a string for `text`; an ISO 8601 string for `datetime`.
- **References are flat**: a run carries `"machine": "linux-x86_64"` and
  `"commit": "abc123"`, not nested objects. `POST /commits/resolve` turns a page
  of commit values into full commits in one call.
- **Compression**: a request body may be gzip-compressed, with
  `Content-Encoding: gzip`; any other coding is 415 `unsupported_encoding`, and
  data that does not decode is 400. Responses are compressed only when the
  request's `Accept-Encoding` asks for it: plain `curl` gets plain JSON, and
  `curl --compressed` decodes what it asked for.

## Authentication

Send `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Scopes form a hierarchy -- `read` <
`submit` < `triage` < `manage` < `admin` -- and a key grants its own scope and
every lower one. `read` endpoints allow anonymous access, so send no header if
you only read. A header that carries no usable Bearer token, or an unknown or
revoked one, is 401 even on a `read` endpoint, and too little scope is 403. A
key may be restricted (its `restricted_to` list) to whole projects, each
`{"project": ..., "suite": null}`, and single suites, each `{"project": ...,
"suite": ...}`, and then has its scope only in the suites it covers: those it
lists, and every suite of the projects it lists, including suites created there
later. A restricted key can create a suite in a project, move a suite into it,
or change its display name, only if it lists the project as a whole. Creating,
renaming and deleting projects need an unrestricted key. Renames and moves leave
keys alone: a key listing a suite still covers it under its new names, and a key
listing a project covers whatever suites the project holds now, so a move takes
a suite from the keys listing its old project and gives it to those listing the
new one. Deleting a project or a suite removes it from the keys that list it,
and one created later under its name is not covered; a key left with nothing
listed can only read. To check a token before relying on it,
`GET /api/auth` returns the key it belongs to, including the scope it grants and
its `restricted_to`.

## Workflows

**Create a suite** in a project, which must exist: create the project first if
need be, with `POST /api/projects` and a body such as `{"name": "llvm"}`, then
post the suite's schema to `POST /api/projects/{project}/suites`.

**Rename or move a suite** with `PATCH /api/projects/{project}/suites/{suite}`
and a body such as `{"name": "microbenchmarks"}`, `{"project": "llvm"}` or both;
rename a project with `PATCH /api/projects/{project}` and `{"name": ...}`. Only
names change: the data stays. The old names are not kept as aliases, so every
URL and every bot using them gets 404 until it is updated.

Paths below are relative to `/api/projects/{project}/suites/{suite}`. Metric and
field names in the examples are placeholders: use the ones the suite's schema
declares.

**Submit a run** with `POST /runs`:

```json
{
  "format_version": "5",
  "machine": {"name": "linux-x86_64", "fields": {"os": "linux"}},
  "commit": {"value": "abc123", "ordinal": 593922, "fields": {"author": "Jane Doe"}},
  "run_parameters": {"build_config": "Release"},
  "tests": [
    {"name": "bench/foo", "samples": [{"execution_time": 1.23, "compile_time": 0.45}]},
    {"name": "bench/bar", "samples": [
      {"execution_time": 0.10, "compile_time": 0.40},
      {"execution_time": 0.11},
      {"execution_time": 0.12}
    ]}
  ]
}
```

The machine and the commit are created if they do not exist. Each test has one
entry, whose `samples` hold one object per repetition, with the metrics that
repetition has a value for: above, `bench/bar` ran three times, and
`compile_time` was measured once. `uuid` is optional and generated when
omitted. `measured_at`, when the run was measured, is optional too: it defaults
to the time the server receives the run, which is recorded as `submitted_at`.
The submission is atomic, and answers 201 with the run. A run cannot be changed afterwards.
It never overwrites what is stored: a field, tag or ordinal that differs from
the stored one is 409, and `PATCH` is the only way to change it. The machine's
`tracked` flag is the exception: it is set only when the submission creates the
machine, and ignored rather than compared afterwards.

**Compress a large submission** whole, which typically shrinks it several
times over. curl does not compress a request body itself; compress it first, and
send it with `--data-binary`, which sends it byte for byte:

```
gzip -c run.json | curl --data-binary @- -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Content-Encoding: gzip' -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  "$LNT_URL/api/projects/llvm/suites/nts/runs"
```

**Submit a throwaway experiment**, such as the A/B runs of a pull request, on a
commit with no ordinal (e.g. `"value": "pr-1234"`), and on a machine of its own
if it measures a configuration no existing machine has. Give that commit and
machine `"delete_after_inactive_days": 30` in the submission: the server
deletes each of them, with its runs, once no run has been submitted for it in
that many days. A commit with an ordinal is never deleted that way. Like
`tracked`, the setting is only used when the submission creates the machine or
the commit; `PATCH` changes or clears it afterwards. Submit such a machine with
`"tracked": false` as well: it then stays out of dashboards, and the web UI
lists it after the machines LNT monitors wherever a machine is picked, so that
experiments don't crowd them.

**Read a machine's history** with
`GET /series?machine=linux-x86_64&metric=execution_time`. It streams every value
of the metric on that machine as newline-delimited JSON, unpaginated, one
sample per line:

```json
{"test": "bench/foo", "machine": "linux-x86_64", "metric": "execution_time",
 "value": 1.23, "commit": "abc123", "ordinal": 593922, "tag": null,
 "run_uuid": "573af861-8303-4a5b-a643-b8321e0142c4",
 "submitted_at": "2026-08-25T14:22:41Z", "measured_at": "2026-08-25T14:02:17Z"}
```

Lines come by test name, then by ordinal, with the commits without one last.
Narrow it down with `test=` (`&test=bench/foo` to chart one test; repeat it for
a few tests, which lengthen the URL), `commit`, `after_commit`, `before_commit`,
the run's `submitted_after`, `submitted_before`, `measured_after` and
`measured_before`, and `has_ordinal` (`true` for only the commits with an
ordinal, `false` for only those without).
Ask for it compressed (`curl --compressed`). If the download is interrupted --
the machine deleted, a schema change, a server restart -- the connection is
closed before the end of the response, which `curl --fail` reports with a
non-zero status: download again.

**Get an overview across machines** with
`GET /trends?metric=execution_time&machine=a&machine=b&last_n=100`. It returns
one `value` per (machine, commit), for the `last_n` most recent commits by
ordinal that have data. Each test's samples in a run are reduced by
`sample_agg` (`median` by default), the run's geomean is taken across tests, and
the runs at a commit are combined by another geomean. The metric must be
numeric.

**Follow up on a data point** through its `run_uuid`: `GET /runs/{uuid}`,
`GET /runs/{uuid}/samples?test=bench/foo`, and `GET /runs/{uuid}/profiles`. A
profile is then read through its own UUID; every counter is a raw count.
`GET /profiles/{uuid}/document` returns it whole, as plain JSON: gzip-compressed
and base64-encoded, it is a test entry's `profile` again.

**Compare a run with the previous commit on its machine**:
`GET /commits?machine=linux-x86_64&before_commit=abc123&sort=-ordinal&limit=1`
returns the nearest earlier commit at which that machine has runs, which the
commit's own `previous` may not be, and
`GET /runs?machine=linux-x86_64&commit={value}` lists those runs.

**Check what is already tracked** before recording a regression. A change is
tracked when a regression attributed to its commit has an indicator naming its
machine, test and metric. Check many at once with
`POST /regressions/indicators/query`:

```json
{"machine": ["linux-x86_64"], "test": ["bench/foo", "bench/bar"],
 "metric": "execution_time", "commit": "abc123"}
```

Every key is optional; `machine`, `test` and `state` are lists. It returns the
matching indicators across all regressions, each as `{uuid, regression_uuid,
machine, test, metric}`, cursor-paginated with `cursor` and `limit` in the body:
a (machine, test, metric) it returns is already tracked at that commit. Read a
regression itself with `GET /regressions/{uuid}`.

**Record a regression** with `POST /regressions`:

```json
{"title": "foo slowdown", "commit": "abc123",
 "indicators": [{"machine": "linux-x86_64", "test": "bench/foo", "metric": "execution_time"}]}
```

Every key is optional; `bug`, `notes` and `state` are accepted too. The state
defaults to `detected`, and moves freely between `detected`, `active`,
`not_to_be_fixed`, `fixed` and `false_positive` through `PATCH`. As for a run,
`uuid` is optional and generated when omitted; choose your own to make the
request safe to retry.
